newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares pause, but bulls still prevail.
newsitem.headline: German shares pause, but bulls still prevail.

text.p: EMU worries and weak signals from the U.S. and Japan dragged German shares off all-time highs on Friday, but dealers said the market was still poised for further gains next week.

Despite Friday's 0.5 percent drop to 3,259.64 points, the 30-share DAX index has still risen more than two percent this week. Its record close on Thursday of 3,276.72 points represented a 13 percent rise this year.
And many dealers say more is to come, given that analysts are still in the process of upgrading earnings estimates for German firms in the light of the dollar's dramatic rally.
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day electronic trade in the 30 blue chips, was down five points at 3,267.50 points at 1501 GMT.
"What we've seen today was no real pressure. Investors were hardly there at all," said a senior trader at a Bavarian bank.
A Frankfurt dealer said: "I can see more money coming into the market next week. Things should be at least stable with a positive leaning."
Dealers also conceded that market rumours of a statement on a delayed launch of the euro were unrealistic.

Talk of such a statement, to which no market players could ascribe a clear source, had sent prices lower in early bourse trading, as dealers feared that an EMU delay could hurt earnings prospects for exporters.
The decline halted after the Bundesbank and the Finance Ministry denied any such plans, but the thinly-traded market lacked impetus for another advance, dealers said.
Performance was uneven, with a few clear exceptions. Retailer Metro AG was up nearly five percent at 148.70 marks in late trade, after dealers said the stock had broken above a key technical barrier.
